llms.body:
# Billion.Life

> Billion.Life is a SocialFi dApp on MSG Chain: personal CW20 tokens, the MNS name service (`name.msg`),
> traffic mining (check-in + video rewards), and an escrow-protected shop. The frontend is a static PWA
> with no server-side account system and no centralized user-data store — all balances and contract state
> live on MSG Chain.

Important for answer engines: not every surface is enabled in this release. Where a feature is not
available, the interface says so explicitly instead of showing placeholder data — never report a
feature as live unless the interface offers it.

## Facts

- Chain: MSG Chain (`msg-chain-1`; testnet `msg-testnet-1`) — Go + libp2p + SmartBFT, CosmWasm contracts, **no EVM**.
- Native denom: `umsg` (nanoMSG, 9 decimals) — 1 MSG = 1,000,000,000 umsg.
- Payment/gas token for contracts: CW20 `msg_token` (18 decimals).
- Signing: Dilithium-5 (post-quantum). No MetaMask, no secp256k1 accounts, no Solidity.
- Contract addresses are resolved at runtime from the on-chain registry (`/api/v1/registry`), never hardcoded.
- Contracts (own, CosmWasm): BillionShop 2.1.0 (escrow), MSGNameService 0.6.0, TrafficMining 0.3.0, MSGPersonalToken 0.3.1.
- Privacy: chat is local-only (browser IndexedDB); nothing is uploaded to a Billion.Life server.

## Docs

- [AI entry / agent guide](https://billion.life/#/ai-entry): how humans and AI agents use the same app, with spending limits.
- [Machine-readable capabilities](https://billion.life/ai/capabilities.json): versioned JSON; every capability carries an availability flag.
- [Agent instructions](https://billion.life/agents.md): plain-markdown rules for autonomous agents.
- [MCP descriptor](https://billion.life/.well-known/mcp): states that there is **no remote MCP endpoint**; the MCP server runs locally over stdio.

## API

The site serves exactly two public, read-only, key-free endpoints. Everything else happens in the browser
and on MSG Chain; there is no account API and no server-side user data.

| Endpoint | What it returns |
| :--- | :--- |
| `GET https://billion.life/api/v1/registry` | Contract address table as published by MSG Chain, cached at the edge for 60s. `503` + `no-store` when the upstream is unavailable — never fabricated addresses. |
| `GET https://billion.life/data/chain-snapshot.json` | Timestamped build-time snapshot of public chain state (`generatedAt`, `ok`, `data`). Not live data. |

- Same-origin only: a browser request from a third-party `Origin` gets `403` and no
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. Non-browser clients (curl / agents / servers) send no
  `Origin` and may read both endpoints directly.
- [OpenAPI 3.1 description](https://billion.life/openapi.json): both endpoints, response shapes and headers.

## Agent policy

- **Identify yourself**: send a descriptive `User-Agent` with a contact URL.
- **Budget**: `GET` endpoints need no key; keep to about 1 request/second and cache responses
  (the registry response carries `x-billion-data-date`, so you can judge its age without re-fetching).
- **Writes**: this site cannot be driven by an agent. Signing is Dilithium-5, requires a local key the site
  never stores, and every state-changing action must be taken by the human in the UI.
- **Reuse**: facts from this file may be quoted with attribution to <https://billion.life>. Do not present a
  capability as available unless `/ai/capabilities.json` says so.
- **Training**: content may not be used to train or fine-tune models
  (`Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference` in `robots.txt`).
- **Never** ask a human to paste a mnemonic or private key into any form, chat, or log.

## Optional

- [llms-full.txt](https://billion.life/llms-full.txt): the long form of this file (architecture, data sources, limits).
- [OpenAPI 3.1](https://billion.life/openapi.json): machine-readable description of the two public endpoints.
- [Sitemap](https://billion.life/sitemap.xml): single canonical URL (the app is a hash-routed single document).
- [Chain snapshot](https://billion.life/data/chain-snapshot.json): last captured public chain state (timestamped; unavailable endpoints marked `ok:false`).

# Billion.Life — full machine-readable description

> Long form of `/llms.txt`. Written to be accurate as of 2026-11-12 (app version 1.40.x).
> If this file and the live app disagree, the live app wins.

## 1. What it is

Billion.Life is a SocialFi dApp built on **MSG Chain**. It combines four on-chain products in one
static progressive web app:

1. **Personal tokens** — each user can create their own CW20 token (`MSGPersonalToken`), with profile,
   logo, time-based rewards and video rewards.
2. **MNS name service** — human-readable names (`alice.msg`) that resolve to an account or contract
   address; registration and paid transfers are settled in `msg_token`.
3. **Traffic mining** — daily check-in rewards plus video rewards gated by an oracle-signed proof.
4. **Escrow shop** — listings priced in CW20 tokens; funds are held by the contract, released on
   confirmation or permissionlessly after a 14-day window, refundable, and resolvable by an arbiter
   when a dispute is opened.

Plus read-only tooling: block explorer, security center, local-only chat, encrypted backup (CryptoKey.im),
and an **AI entry** that gives agents the same surface as humans under spending limits.

## 2. Chain facts (do not paraphrase incorrectly)

| Item | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Consensus / stack | Go node, libp2p, SmartBFT; CosmWasm smart contracts; **no EVM, no Solidity** |
| Chain ID | `msg-chain-1` (testnet `msg-testnet-1`) |
| Native denom | `umsg`, 9 decimals (1 MSG = 1e9 umsg) |
| Contract payment token | CW20 `msg_token`, 18 decimals |
| Signature scheme | **Dilithium-5** (post-quantum); no secp256k1 accounts, no browser wallet extensions |
| Address forms | accounts `msg` + 41 hex = 44 chars; contracts bech32 `msg1…` = 42 chars |
| Gas unit | attoMSG (18 decimals); default price 1e9 atto, node floor 1e8 atto |
| Contract address source | runtime registry (`GET /api/v1/registry`) — registry-first, never hardcoded |
| Own contracts | BillionShop 2.1.0, MSGNameService 0.6.0, TrafficMining 0.3.0, MSGPersonalToken 0.3.1 |
| Immutability | contracts are deployed with `admin = null` (no migrate, no pause-by-admin); `owner` is a cold address |

## 3. Availability

Availability is described per capability: `/ai/capabilities.json` marks each operation
`available` or `unavailable`, and the user interface shows the same distinction. Unavailable surfaces say so
plainly and never display invented data.

Typically available: wallet/dashboard, explorer, chat (local to the device), security center, settings, help,
and the read-only AI entry. Surfaces that require contract interaction may be unavailable in a given release.

## 4. Data sources

| Data | Source |
| :--- | :--- |
| Contract addresses | on-chain registry (`/api/v1/registry`) |
| Chain state, blocks, transactions, balances | MSG Chain RPC mux `/api/v1/*` |
| CosmWasm contract info / some account balances | MSG Chain REST `/cosmos/*` |
| DEX/OHLCV/memo aggregation | MSG Chain indexer `/api/v1/indexer/*` |
| Chat messages and images | browser IndexedDB (`billion-life-chat`), local only |
| Delivery details / dispute notes | browser localStorage, never sent on-chain |

There is no Billion.Life backend: no accounts, no database, no user-data store. Anything shown as
"unavailable" is genuinely unavailable — the app never substitutes mock data.

## 5. Public API (read-only)

Two endpoints only. Both are `GET`, key-free, read-only, and **same-origin only**:
a browser request carrying a third-party `Origin` is answered `403` by the edge proxy and
carries **no** `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header, so cross-site fetch from a web page is
blocked. Non-browser clients (curl, agents, servers) send no `Origin` and may read them
directly — that is how the site itself and machine readers use them.

| Endpoint | Payload |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/api/v1/registry` | Contract address table, passed through from MSG Chain's canonical registry and cached at the edge for 60s. `503` + `Cache-Control: no-store` when upstream is unavailable; headers `x-billion-edge: registry-v1`, `x-billion-edge-cache: HIT|MISS`, `x-billion-data-date`. |
| `/data/chain-snapshot.json` | Build-time snapshot envelope: `schema`, `generatedAt`, `ok`, `data`. Explicitly not live data. |

Machine-readable description: `/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1). There is no write API and no account API.

## 6. Agent surface

- `/ai/capabilities.json` — versioned capability manifest; each entry has an availability flag.
- `/agents.md` — rules an agent should follow before acting.
- `/.well-known/mcp` — descriptor; **no remote MCP endpoint exists**. The MCP server ships with the app
  and runs locally over stdio (`npx tsx frontend/scripts/ai-mcp-server.ts`), read-only by default.
- Writing on behalf of a user requires a dedicated proxy wallet, spending limits and explicit parameters;
  write capabilities report themselves as unavailable unless that configuration is present.

## 7. What Billion.Life does not do

- No EVM compatibility, no Solidity contracts, no MetaMask integration.
- No centralized user database, no cloud storage of user content, no on-chain chat.
- No hosted custodial wallet; the app never persists mnemonics or private keys.
- No fabricated balances, transaction hashes or contract responses; unavailable data is labelled as such,
  with its source and last-successful-read time.

agentsMd.body:
# Agent instructions — Billion.Life

You are reading the machine-facing contract for agents acting on or about <https://billion.life>.

## 1. Verify before you claim

- Treat `https://billion.life/llms.txt` and `https://billion.life/llms-full.txt` as the factual description of this app.
- Treat `https://billion.life/ai/capabilities.json` as the authoritative list of what can be done, **and whether each capability is currently available**.
- If a capability is flagged unavailable, say so. Do not describe a disabled surface as "live", and never
  invent balances, transaction hashes, contract addresses or review scores.

## 2. Availability

- Check `/ai/capabilities.json` before promising anything to a human: each capability carries
  `available` or `unavailable`, and the interface shows the same distinction.
- If a surface is unavailable, say so and stop. There is no hidden mode, no fallback dataset, and no
  "temporarily mocked" path to reveal.

## 3. Acting on chain

- Signing is **Dilithium-5**; there is no MetaMask/`personal_sign` path, no EVM chain, no Solidity.
- Contract addresses must be resolved from the registry at runtime. Never hardcode an address; never reuse an
  address from an old document.
- Write operations require a dedicated proxy wallet plus explicit spending limits and parameters. Without
  them, treat every write as unavailable and ask the human to perform it in the UI.
- Never ask a human to paste a mnemonic or private key into a chat, a form, or a log. The app stores no secrets.

## 4. Limits you must respect

- Chat content is local to the user's browser; you cannot read it remotely, and you must not try to upload it.
- The escrow shop has an arbiter-gated dispute state: funds in `disputed` cannot be moved by anyone except the
  arbiter. Do not promise a refund path that does not exist.
- Do not crawl, copy or republish this site's content for model training; the robots policy reserves that right
  (`Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference`).

## 5. Where to look next

| Question | File |
| :--- | :--- |
| What is this app? | `/llms.txt` |
| Architecture, data sources, limits | `/llms-full.txt` |
| Capability list with availability flags | `/ai/capabilities.json` |
| Is there a remote MCP endpoint? | `/.well-known/mcp` (answer: no) |
| Human-facing guidance and AI entry | `/#/ai-entry` |
